rd.text: The effective tax rate reflects the recognition of certain tax benefits in the financial statements including those benefits from tax-exempt interest income, federal low-income housing tax credits, renewable energy tax credits, research and development tax credits, historic tax credits and excess tax benefits from recognized stock compensation. These tax benefits are offset by the tax effect of stock-based compensation expense and a provision for state income tax expense. We frequently analyze our projections of taxable income and make adjustments to our provision for income taxes accordingly.

prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
We maintain the allowance for credit losses at an appropriate level based on our assessment of estimable and expected losses related to various portfolios subject to credit risk. Our allowance for credit losses (ACL) is based on our historical loss experience that includes the inherent risk of our loans and leases, HTM securities, and other account receivables, along with various other factors including but not limited to, collateral values, trends in asset quality, level of delinquent loans and concentrations, consideration of past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts. Further, regional and national economic forecasts are considered in our expected credit losses on loans and leases. Our evaluation is based on a review of the portfolio and requires significant, complex and difficult judgments.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded a provision for credit losses of $8.4 million, an increase of $1.8 million, compared to $6.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The current quarter provision for credit losses was driven by a specific reserve on a student housing-related loan.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Three months ended September 30, 2026 : During the three months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense was $161.6 million, a decrease of $1.5 million from $163.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a $5.5 million decrease in other operating expense primarily driven by lower external fraud losses and Cash Connect ® external funding costs as well as a $1.4 million decrease in professional fees primarily driven by a recovery of previously incurred legal expenses. These decreases were partially offset by a $2.2 million increase in salaries and benefits primarily related to merit increases, a $1.7 million increase in equipment expenses from client transaction costs in Wealth and Trust and continued investment in technology across the franchise, as well as a $1.3 million increase in loan workout and other credit costs primarily due to the write-down of an existing OREO property.

Nine months ended September 30, 2026: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense was $490.6 million, an increase of $16.4 million from $474.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonop.text:
Three months ended September 30, 2026 : During the three months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense was $161.6 million, a decrease of $1.5 million from $163.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a $5.5 million decrease in other operating expense primarily driven by lower external fraud losses and Cash Connect ® external funding costs as well as a $1.4 million decrease in professional fees primarily driven by a recovery of previously incurred legal expenses. These decreases were partially offset by a $2.2 million increase in salaries and benefits primarily related to merit increases, a $1.7 million increase in equipment expenses from client transaction costs in Wealth and Trust and continued investment in technology across the franchise, as well as a $1.3 million increase in loan workout and other credit costs primarily due to the write-down of an existing OREO property.

Nine months ended September 30, 2026: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense was $490.6 million, an increase of $16.4 million from $474.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We and our subsidiaries file a consolidated federal income tax return and separate state income tax returns. Income taxes are accounted for in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes , which requires the recording of deferred income taxes for tax consequences of temporary differences. We recorded income tax expense of $28.3 million and $82.7 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to income tax expense of $24.4 million and $68.8 million for the same periods in 2025. The increase for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods in 2025 was primarily due to higher income before taxes in 2026.

Our effective tax rate was 24.1% for both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to 24.2% and 24.3% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The reduction was primarily due to increased federal tax credits.

The effective tax rate reflects the recognition of certain tax benefits in the financial statements including those benefits from tax-exempt interest income, federal low-income housing tax credits, renewable energy tax credits, research and development tax credits, historic tax credits and excess tax benefits from recognized stock compensation.

(1) Weighted average yields for tax-exempt securities and loans have been computed on a tax-equivalent basis.

(2) Average balances are net of unearned income and include nonperforming loans.

(3) Includes commercial mortgage and commercial construction loans.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Three months ended September 30, 2026: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest income was $91.0 million, an increase of $4.5 million from $86.5 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase was driven by $12.4 million of higher Wealth and Trust fees, including WSFS Institutional Services ® , BMT-DE, and Private Wealth Management. These increases were partially offset by a $3.6 million decrease in Cash Connect ® , primarily due to the impact of interest rates and lower ATM volumes, and lower fees from mortgage and SBA loans as we retained more of our originated loans.

Nine months ended September 30, 2026: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest income was $271.1 million, an increase of $15.7 million from $255.4 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was primarily driven by $30.4 million of higher Wealth and Trust fees, partially offset by a $8.4 million decrease in Cash Connect ® for the reasons mentioned above, a $4.1 million impairment of one of our equity investments, and $2.3 million of earnout revenue from Spring EQ recognized in the prior year.

For further information, see Note 2 to the unaudited Consolidated Financial Statements.

intro.text: WSFS Financial Corporation (the Company or WSFS) is a savings and loan holding company headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware. Substantially all of our assets are held by the Company's subsidiary, Wilmington Savings Fund Society, FSB (WSFS Bank or the Bank), one of the ten oldest bank and trust companies in the United States (U.S.) continuously operating under the same name. As a federal savings bank that was formerly chartered as a state mutual savings bank, WSFS Bank enjoys a broader scope of permissible activities than most other financial institutions. With $21.3 billion in assets and $97.4 billion in assets under management (AUM) and assets under administration (AUA) at December 31, 2025, WSFS Bank is the oldest and largest locally-managed bank and trust company headquartered in the Greater Philadelphia and Delaware region.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.
